pages.fact: Johannes Gutenberg finished his printed Bible in Mainz around 1455, using movable metal type.
Martin Luther circulated his Ninety-five Theses in Wittenberg in 1517, attacking the sale of indulgences.
The Peace of Augsburg in 1555 let each German prince choose the religion of his territory, summed up as cuius regio, eius religio.
The Council of Trent met between 1545 and 1563 and reaffirmed Catholic doctrine while reforming clerical training through seminaries.
The historian Alfred Crosby coined the term Columbian Exchange in 1972 to describe the transfer of plants, animals and diseases across the Atlantic.
Potatoes and maize from the Americas raised calorie yields per acre in Europe and China, supporting population growth after 1700.
Smallpox reached Hispaniola by 1518, and epidemics killed a large share of Indigenous populations within a century of contact.
The silver mountain of Potosi, in present-day Bolivia, supplied Spanish coins that paid for Chinese silk and porcelain through Manila after 1571.
Nicolaus Copernicus published On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres in 1543, placing the Sun rather than the Earth at the centre.
Galileo Galilei turned a telescope to the sky in 1609 and reported four moons orbiting Jupiter in his Starry Messenger of 1610.
Francis Bacon argued in the Novum Organum of 1620 that knowledge should be built by induction from organised experiment.
Isaac Newton's Principia of 1687 stated three laws of motion and a law of universal gravitation that covered both falling apples and orbiting planets.
Immanuel Kant answered the question What is Enlightenment in 1784 with the motto Sapere aude, dare to know.
John Locke's Two Treatises of Government, published in 1689, argued that rulers hold power in trust to protect life, liberty and property.
Montesquieu's The Spirit of the Laws in 1748 proposed separating legislative, executive and judicial powers so that each could check the others.
pages.query: Montesquieu Spirit of the Laws separation

pages.fact: Denis Diderot and Jean d'Alembert edited the Encyclopedie, whose first volume appeared in Paris in 1751.
The Estates-General met at Versailles in May 1789 for the first time since 1614, called to solve a royal debt crisis.
Parisians stormed the Bastille on 14 July 1789, and in August the Assembly abolished feudal privileges.
The Committee of Public Safety, dominated by Maximilien Robespierre, directed the Terror of 1793 and 1794 until his fall in the month of Thermidor.
pages.query: Committee of Public Safety Robespierre Thermidor

pages.fact: Napoleon Bonaparte seized power in the coup of 18 Brumaire in November 1799 and issued the Civil Code in 1804.
Abundant coal near navigable water, high wages and cheap energy made labour-saving machines pay in Britain earlier than elsewhere.
James Watt patented a separate condenser in 1769, which cut the fuel a steam engine burned and made it useful beyond coal mines.
Richard Arkwright opened a water-powered cotton spinning mill at Cromford in 1771, an early model of the factory system.
Luddites broke stocking frames and power looms in Nottinghamshire and Yorkshire between 1811 and 1816 to protest falling wages.
Aerobic respiration yields roughly 30 to 32 ATP per glucose, far more than the 2 ATP from glycolysis alone.
Glycolysis takes place in the cytosol and splits one glucose into two pyruvate molecules without using oxygen.
The citric acid cycle, also called the Krebs cycle, runs in the mitochondrial matrix and releases carbon dioxide.
ATP synthase uses a proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane to make ATP, a process called chemiosmosis.
A sampling distribution is the distribution of a statistic, such as the sample mean, over all possible samples of the same size.
pages.query: sampling distribution statistic all possible samples

pages.fact: The standard error of the mean equals the population standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size.
pages.query: standard error square root sample size

pages.fact: The central limit theorem says the sample mean is approximately normal for large samples, whatever the shape of the population, with n of at least 30 as a common rule of thumb.
A 95 percent confidence interval for a mean is the sample mean plus or minus about 1.96 standard errors.
